rows.question: For the RBAC action 'access_as_shared' (considering only IPv4 subnets), what are the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP version with subtotals and a grand total, and—alongside those stats—what are the top 3 shared networks by subnet count, including each network ID, its subnet count, and the tenant ID of each subnet (with repeated network IDs suppressed)? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH subnet_versions AS (
    SELECT
        s.id AS subnet_id,
        s.ip_version
    FROM subnets s
    JOIN networks n ON s.network_id = n.id
    WHERE n.status = 'active'
      AND n.admin_state_up = 1
      AND n.standard_attr_id IS NOT NULL
      AND s.ip_version = 4
),
subnet_counts AS (
    SELECT
        subnet_id,
        COUNT(*) AS subnet_count
    FROM subnet_versions
    GROUP BY subnet_id
),
ranked_networks AS (
    SELECT
        subnet_id,
        subnet_count,
        tenant_id
    FROM subnet_counts
    ORDER BY subnet_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
)
SELECT
    AVG(sv.ip_version) AS avg_ip_version,
    VAR_POPULATION_STDDEV(sv.ip_version) AS variance_ip_version,
    STDDEV_POPULATION(sv.ip_version) AS stddev_ip_version,
    COUNT(*) AS total_subnets,
    (
        SELECT
            COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id)
        FROM subnets
        WHERE network_id IN (
            SELECT
                subnet_id
            FROM ranked_networks
        )
    ) AS total_tenants,
    (
        SELECT
            network_id
        FROM ranked_networks
        ORDER BY subnet_count DESC
    ) AS top_3_network_ids
FROM subnet_versions sv
GROUP BY sv.ip_version
ORDER BY avg_ip_version

rows.question: For tenants that are in the top 10 by distinct DOWN ports and also in the top 10 by IPv4 subnet count, return the tenant ID, total distinct DOWN ports, whether any of those DOWN ports have an IP allocation, total IPv4 subnets, and whether any IPv4 subnet has a standard attribute record with a non-null updated-at timestamp—keeping only tenants where DOWN ports are more than 75% of their IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH tenant_subnet_counts AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(id) AS ipv4_subnets
  FROM subnets
  WHERE ip_version = 4
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
tenant_port_counts AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS distinct_down_ports
  FROM ports
  WHERE admin_state_up = 0
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
top_ten_tenants_ports AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id
  FROM ports
  WHERE status = 'down'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  ORDER BY COUNT(id) DESC
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
  t.tenant_id,
  tpc.distinct_down_ports,
  tsc.ipv4_subnets,
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)
    FROM ipallocations
    WHERE port_id IN (
      SELECT
        port_id
      FROM ports
      WHERE tenant_id = t.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS has_ip_allocation,
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)
    FROM subnetpools
    WHERE tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND standard_attr_id IS NOT NULL
  ) AS has_updated_attribute
FROM
  top_ten_tenants_ports t
JOIN
  tenant_port_counts tpc ON t.tenant_id = tpc.tenant_id
JOIN
  tenant_subnet_counts tsc ON t.tenant_id = tsc.tenant_id
WHERE
  tpc.distinct_down_ports > 0.75 * tsc.ipv4_subnets

rows.question: How many distinct admin_state_up = 1 ports that are bound to a security group are there, and how many distinct DOWN ports belong to security groups whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per security group? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH aggregate_down_ports_per_group AS (
  SELECT
    sg.id AS security_group_id,
    AVG(
      CASE
        WHEN f.status = 'DOWN' THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS average_down_port_count
  FROM securitygroups AS sg
  INNER JOIN firewalls AS f
    ON sg.id = f.firewall_policy_id
  GROUP BY sg.id
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS distinct_up_ports,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS distinct_down_ports
FROM ports AS p
JOIN securitygroupportbindings AS sgb
  ON p.id = sgb.port_id
JOIN securitygroups AS sg
  ON sgb.security_group_id = sg.id
JOIN aggregate_down_ports_per_group AS adppg
  ON sg.id = adppg.security_group_id
JOIN ports AS dp
  ON dp.id = sgb.port_id
WHERE
  dp.admin_state_up = 1 AND adppg.average_down_port_count > adppg.average_down_port_count

rows.question: For external networks that are marked as default (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list each network’s ID, name, status, and ADMIN_STATE_UP, along with (1) the per-status average ADMIN_STATE_UP computed as a window over networks ordered by name, (2) the overall average of those per-status averages across all statuses, and (3) the overall benchmark ADMIN_STATE_UP across all such external networks and a category showing whether each network is ABOVE_BENCHMARK, BELOW_BENCHMARK, or AT_BENCHMARK versus that benchmark. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  n.id,
  n.name,
  n.status,
  n.admin_state_up,
  AVG(n.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY n.status) AS avg_admin_state_up,
  AVG(avg_admin_state_up) OVER () AS overall_avg_admin_state_up,
  CASE
    WHEN n.admin_state_up > (
      AVG(n.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY n.status)
    ) THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK'
    WHEN n.admin_state_up < (
      AVG(n.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY n.status)
    ) THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK'
    ELSE 'AT_BENCHMARK'
  END AS benchmark_category
FROM externalnetworks n
WHERE n.is_default = 0
ORDER BY n.name

rows.question: For IPv4 subnets that are in the top 10 by DNS nameserver order range and that have DNS nameservers configured, return the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first and last IP (only where the first IP is the minimum for that subnet), the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows by subnet ID, plus the DNS nameserver order range and order variance. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  s.name AS subnet_name,
  s.tenant_id,
  s.network_id,
  s.ip_version,
  s.cidr,
  s.gateway_ip,
  s.enable_dhcp,
  ipap.first_ip,
  ipap.last_ip,
  s.standard_attr_id,
  (s.standard_attr_id - s.standard_attr_id) AS standard_attr_variance,
  (s.standard_attr_id - s.standard_attr_id) AS standard_attr_variance,
  ds.order,
  VAR_POPULATOR(ds.order, 1, 2) AS order_variance
FROM
  subnets s

  ipamallocationpools ipap ON s.id = ipap.id
JOIN
  ipamsubnets is ON s.id = is.id
JOIN
  dnsnameservers ds ON s.id = ds.subnet_id
WHERE
  s.ip_version = 4
  AND s.enable_dhcp = 1
ORDER BY
  ds.order
LIMIT 10

WITH windowed_admin_state_up AS (
  SELECT
    p.port_id,
    pt.tenant_id,
    a.agent_type,
    p.mac_address,
    p.ip_address,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pt.tenant_id ORDER BY p.ip_address) AS row_num,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_down_ports,

  GROUP BY p.port_id, pt.tenant_id, a.agent_type
  ORDER BY p.port_id, p.ip_address
)
SELECT
  *
FROM windowed_admin_state_up

rows.question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with its RBAC action and target tenant (including the distinct RBAC target-tenant count per network and the dense-rank window column), and also include—alongside every such network/RBAC row—the per-(port status, device owner) port counts for ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for each group, and each group’s deviation from the overall average port count. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  n.name AS network_name,
  n.status AS network_status,
  n.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up,
  rbac.rbac_action,
  t.tenant_id AS target_tenant_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT rbac.rbac_action) AS distinct_rbac_count,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY rbac.rbac_action) AS dense_rank,
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(p.id)
    FROM ports AS p
    WHERE
      p.standard_attr_id = 'ports' AND p.network_id = n.id
  ) AS port_count,
  (
    SELECT
      STDDEV(
        (
          SELECT
            COUNT(p.id)
          FROM ports AS p
          WHERE
            p.standard_attr_id = 'ports' AND p.network_id = n.id
        )
      )
    FROM networks AS n
  ) AS port_count_variance
FROM networks AS n
JOIN bgp_speakers AS b ON n.id = b.network_id
JOIN bgp_speakers_networks AS rbac ON b.id = rbac.bgp_speaker_id
JOIN ports AS p ON p.network_id = n.id
WHERE
  n.status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY
  n.id,
  n.name,
  n.status,
  n.admin_state_up,
  rbac.rbac_action
ORDER BY
  n.id

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN and that also have a standard attribute ID above the average for their resource type, list each port’s port ID and tenant ID along with host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the IP-address-ordered row number (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the overall average DOWN-port count benchmark and the tenant usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), plus the port’s MAC address and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within its resource type. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH down_ports_by_tenant AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    AVG(id) AS average_down_port_id
  FROM ports
  WHERE status = 'down'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
down_ports AS (
  SELECT
    p.port_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    n.name AS host,
    'port' AS vif_type,
    ip.ip_address AS allocated_ip_address,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ip.ip_address) AS ip_address_ordered_row_number,
    COUNT(p.port_id) AS tenant_down_port_count,
    (SELECT AVG(average_down_port_id) FROM down_ports_by_tenant) AS overall_average_down_port_count,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(p.port_id) >= (SELECT AVG(average_down_port_id) FROM down_ports_by_tenant) * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER'
      WHEN COUNT(p.port_id) >= (SELECT AVG(average_down_port_id) FROM down_ports_by_tenant) * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER'
      ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER'
    END AS tenant_usage_category,
    p.mac_address,
    SUM(p.standard_attr_id) OVER (PARTITION BY p.resource_type) AS running_sum_standard_attr_id
  FROM ports AS p
  JOIN ipallocations AS ip ON p.port_id = ip.port_id
  JOIN networks AS n ON ip.network_id = n.id
  WHERE p.status = 'down'
  AND p.standard_attr_id > (SELECT AVG(average_down_port_id) FROM down_ports_by_tenant)
  GROUP BY p.port_id, p.tenant_id, n.name, 'port', ip.ip_address, p.mac_address
)
SELECT
  *
FROM
  down_ports
ORDER BY
  ip_address_ordered_row_number

rows.question: How many DOWN ports have IP allocations (from the DOWN-port per-network allocation analysis) and how many administratively up ports have port security bindings (from the admin-up port security benchmark analysis)? Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each port as 'HIGH_SECURITY' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SECURITY' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SECURITY'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH port_security_bindings AS (
SELECT
  psb.port_id
FROM
  portsecuritybindings AS psb
)
SELECT
  COUNT(CASE WHEN ports.status = 'DOWN' THEN ports.id END) AS down_ports_with_ip_allocations,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN ports.admin_state_up = 1 THEN ports.id END) AS up_ports_with_security_bindings
FROM ports
INNER JOIN port_security_bindings
  ON ports.id = port_security_bindings.port_id

Also include, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average DOWN-port IP allocations per host, and attach the DOWN-status port-security-binding rollup statistics (admin-state label plus the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of port security bindings per port, including subtotal/grand-total style labels). SELECT

  p.tenant_id,
  pb.host,
  v.id AS vif_id,
  ia.ip_address,

rows.question: For each of the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the tenant ID, the total number of such ports, the total number of IP allocations across those ports, whether the tenant has any floating IPs allocated, and the average (across that tenant’s ports) deviation of each port’s IP allocation count from the global average IP allocation count across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH PortAllocations AS (
    SELECT
        p.tenant_id,
        COUNT(ia.port_id) AS total_port_allocations
    FROM ports AS p
    JOIN ipallocations AS ia
        ON p.id = ia.port_id
    WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1
    GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
TenantsWithAllocations AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        total_port_allocations
    FROM PortAllocations
    WHERE total_port_allocations > 0
),
GlobalPortAllocations AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(p.id) AS total_port_allocations
    FROM ports AS p
    WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1
),
TenantsAndAllocations AS (
    SELECT
        t.tenant_id,
        t.total_port_allocations,
        (SELECT AVG(total_port_allocations) FROM TenantsWithAllocations) AS average_deviation,
        CASE
            WHEN t.total_port_allocations > 0 THEN TRUE
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS has_floating_ips
    FROM TenantsWithAllocations t
    ORDER BY t.total_port_allocations DESC
    LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
    tenant_id,
    total_port_allocations,
    average_deviation,
    has_floating_ips
FROM
    TenantsAndAllocations

rows.question: For the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), and where more than 75% of the tenant’s ports are in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, total number of such administratively up ports, total IP allocations across them, whether the tenant has any floating IPs, plus the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is above the DOWN-port average for their resource type and the average running sum of standard attribute IDs for those qualifying DOWN ports. WITH up_ports_by_tenant AS (
  SELECT
    p.tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS up_port_count,
    SUM(s.cidr) AS total_ip_allocations,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_floating_ip
  FROM ports AS p

    ON p.network_id = s.network_id
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
down_ports_by_tenant AS (
  SELECT
    p.tenant_id,
    p.standard_attr_id
  FROM ports AS p
  WHERE p.admin_state_up = 0

avg_down_std_attr AS (

  COUNT(p.id)
FROM `ports` AS p
JOIN `networks` AS n
  ON p.network_id = n.id
WHERE
  p.network_id = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c'
  AND p.standard_attr_id > (
    SELECT

WITH grand_total AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT `subnets`.id) AS `grand_total`
  FROM `subnets`
),
subnet_subtotals AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(ipamsubnets.id) AS subnet_subtotal,
    networks.name AS subnet_name
  FROM networks
  JOIN ipamsubnets
    ON networks.id = ipamsubnets.id
  GROUP BY
    networks.name
),
subnet_attributes AS (
  SELECT
    s.name AS subnet_name,
    s.gateway_ip,
    sa.id AS standard_attr_id,

  JOIN standardattributes sa

),
